name: Lucidity
summary: A headless content management system for sites built in Nuxt, Next.js, React, Vue, or Svelte.
purpose: Gives developers and content teams a CMS layer they can plug into any modern frontend without hard-coding copy. Authors manage schemas and documents; consuming sites read published content over an API.
howItWorks:
An editor signs up, defines content types (authors, pages, posts, or custom schemas), and creates documents. Drafts stay unpublished until explicitly released, so unfinished work never reaches a live site.

When a document is published, Lucidity stores it in Postgres via Prisma and exposes it through a query API gated by API keys. A consuming Nuxt or Next app lists schema types, fetches pages for navigation, and pulls collections such as blog posts onto a page.

The product surface is the CMS itself — sign-up, sign-in, docs, and the API — not a marketing brochure. Sites that only need to demonstrate consumption can point at the Lucidity Demo consumer app.
architecture: Nuxt application for authoring UI, auth, and docs
Draft vs published document lifecycle in the data model
API-key protected query endpoints for headless reads
Schema/type registry so consumers discover content shapes
Optional consumer sites (e.g. Lucidity Demo) as reference integrations
features: Create and edit content types and documents
Keep drafts separate from published documents
Issue and rotate API keys for frontend consumers
Query schema types, pages, and collections over the API
Sign up / sign in for CMS operators
In-app documentation for integrating a frontend
Support Nuxt, Next.js, React, Vue, and Svelte consumers
dataAuth: Operator accounts authenticate to the CMS UI. Published content is readable by clients that present a valid API key. Document drafts, schemas, and key metadata are stored in Postgres; no end-user passwords for consumer sites are stored by Lucidity itself.
deployment: Hosted on Vercel with Supabase as the database/backend. Public docs and API live at lucidity-lac.vercel.app. A separate demo consumer is at lucidity-demo.vercel.app.

name: ProbeWord
summary: An AI SEO brief generator: enter a keyword and optional competitor URLs, and receive work you can put on a page.
purpose: Helps developers and copywriters produce implementable SEO briefs (titles, metas, structure, gaps) instead of historical rank dashboards.
howItWorks:
A user types a search term, optionally adds up to five competitor sites, and picks a market (UK, US, AU, or IE). The form submits to an n8n workflow that calls OpenAI with that context.

The model returns keyword ideas (seed, long-tail, question, comparison), SERP-ready titles, meta descriptions, H1s, slugs, competitor gaps, and on-page recommendations.

The user copies the brief into a CMS or codebase. ProbeWord is not a rank tracker and does not store long historical ranking series as its primary job.
architecture: Nuxt frontend for keyword/competitor input and brief display
n8n workflow orchestration for the research pipeline
OpenAI for keyword clustering and SERP-oriented copy
Market selector (UK, US, AU, IE) passed into the prompt context
Stateless brief generation oriented toward implementable output
features: Run keyword research for a page you intend to publish
Name rival URLs and get a plan to outrank them
Generate titles, meta descriptions, H1s, and slugs
Receive long-tail, question, and comparison keyword ideas
See competitor gaps and on-page recommendations
Choose target market (UK, US, AU, IE)
dataAuth: Brief generation is driven by the submitted keyword, competitors, and market. Session or form input may be held long enough to return a result; there is no public claim of a full account/password store for rank history.
deployment: Deployed on Vercel at probeword.vercel.app. n8n runs the OpenAI workflow used to assemble each brief.

name: BonsAI
summary: An AI plant-based food assistant that builds a week of meals, a grocery list, and leftover ideas in about 30 seconds.
purpose: Helps people eating plant-based food plan a week of meals, shop efficiently, check labels, and reduce waste — with optional premium billing.
howItWorks:
A visitor answers preferences, budget, and time constraints. OpenAI returns a 7-day plant-based plan. The app then produces a shopping list with estimated cost, organised by category.

Extra tools include a label/menu scanner to flag animal ingredients and pantry/leftover suggestions to cut waste. Stripe handles billing: a free tier of five plans a month and premium from £7.99.

Auth and persistent data sit on Neon Postgres via Drizzle. This is a meal-planning product, not a recipe blog.

OpenAI for meal plans, leftover ideas, and label analysis
Stripe Checkout/billing for free vs premium tiers
Client flows for preference intake, plan generation, and shopping lists

Build a grocery list with cost estimates by category
Scan a packet or menu and check it is plant-based
Turn leftovers into another meal
Free tier with a monthly plan allowance

Save preferences for faster regenerations
dataAuth: User accounts and plan history live in Neon. Stripe customer/subscription references are stored for billing state. Preference answers and generated plans are associated with the signed-in user; payment card details stay with Stripe.
deployment: Hosted on Netlify (jbonsai.netlify.app) with Neon Postgres. Stripe manages subscriptions in live/test modes configured for the project.

name: TagFlow
summary: A B2B ordering layer so pet apps, hotels, events, and brands can sell NFC tags on their own sites without running a factory.
purpose: Lets partners sell NFC tags as an add-on without manufacturing hardware themselves. TagFlow sits between the partner storefront and a manufacturer for payment and fulfilment status.
howItWorks:
Partners sign up free, then either embed an iframe checkout or call an API from their own form. A customer on the partner site places a tag order through that surface.

TagFlow takes payment and order status in the middle, then routes fulfilment jobs to a manufacturer. Partners do not need to run a factory or build their own NFC commerce stack.

Typical buyers are pet products, hotels, events, and branded apps that want NFC hardware as an add-on.

Iframe checkout embed for partner sites
API form integration for custom storefronts
features: Partner free sign-up
Embed tag ordering via iframe
Call ordering API from a partner form
Track payment and fulfilment status
Route jobs to a manufacturer
Sell NFC tags without owning a factory
Target pet, hotel, event, and brand use cases
dataAuth: Partner accounts and order records (line items, status, payment references) are stored in the Django app. Manufacturer fulfilment status updates the same order model. Card data is handled by the payment provider, not stored as raw PANs in TagFlow docs.
deployment: Public site at tagflow.co.uk. Django application serves partner portal, API, and checkout embed.

name: UKPubs
summary: A UK-wide pubs and venues directory with search, news, events, and location-based lists.
purpose: Helps people find pubs by town, coast, or football ground, and stay informed about venue news and events across the UK.
howItWorks:
Visitors search by town, county, or pub name. The live site ranks towns and counties by listing count (London has thousands of pubs), lists seaside towns, and shows pubs within a mile of every Premier League stadium.

Alongside directory results, UKPubs publishes pub-industry news and upcoming gigs/comedy at venues. Location services power near-me and stadium-radius lists.

The stack has moved over the years from PHP and Laravel through Python/Nuxt to Nuxt with Supabase and Prisma.

Location/geo queries for town, coast, and stadium radii
Content modules for industry news and venue events
Historical migration path from PHP/Laravel toward Nuxt

name: Zap Task

Cards carry priority, type (bug, feature, story, epic), tags, assignee, due dates, story points, search, and filters. A stats strip shows total, in progress, done, and overdue counts. Dark mode is available.

Realtime updates use Supabase. Multi-tenant hosting can put each team on its own subdomain while the marketing/core app stays at zaptask.co.uk.

Multi-project boards with card metadata model

name: Ball-Z (SiteForge)

Follow-up messages can restyle the theme, rewrite copy, or move sections (pricing, testimonials, services). The user inspects and exports the generated source.

The application generates code; it does not permanently host the customer’s finished production site as a CMS.

This is a try-on visualisation app, not an ecommerce checkout.

name: Exhibitionist / Camme
summary: A live broadcast and chat platform: the public-facing direction of the Camme social cam foundation.
purpose: Enable live broadcast and realtime chat with tipping/purchases. exhibitionist.me is the public product direction of the Camme social cam and chat foundation.
howItWorks:
Built on the Camme social cam and chat foundation — a FastAPI + Go web app with LiveKit video, Redis, Stripe and in-app purchases.

Viewers watch or join a live broadcast with realtime chat. Broadcasters can receive support through tips and purchases; Lovense tip-to-toy hooks are part of the Camme foundation experiments.

exhibitionist.me is the public-facing live broadcast/chat product of that same codebase/idea; Camme remains the underlying social-cam foundation.
architecture: Stripe and in-app purchases for monetisation
Optional Lovense tip-to-toy hooks in the foundation
features: Watch or run a live broadcast
Realtime chat during streams
Tip or purchase to support a broadcaster
Use Camme foundation social-cam capabilities
Experiment with tip-to-toy hardware hooks
dataAuth: Broadcaster and viewer accounts authenticate to the platform. Chat, session, and purchase records are stored server-side. Payment details are handled by Stripe/IAP providers. Redis holds ephemeral realtime state.
deployment: Public product at www.exhibitionist.me. Camme foundation also referenced via camme.vercel.app in related experiments.

name: LocalSEO
summary: Google Maps ranking intelligence by postcode, not city averages — for local operators who need actionable geo SEO.
purpose: Help multi-location and local businesses see Maps ranking heat and competitor movement at postcode granularity, with shareable reports.
howItWorks:
An operator selects locations/postcodes rather than relying on city-wide averages. The app builds heatmaps and tracks competitor movement for those areas.

Weekly alerts and shareable reports summarise multi-location performance so teams can act on local ranking changes.
features: View Maps ranking by postcode
Inspect heatmaps for local visibility
Track competitor movement
Monitor multiple locations
Receive weekly alerts
Share reports with stakeholders
dataAuth: Location configurations and ranking snapshots are stored for the signed-in operator account. Shared reports expose the selected metrics without publishing credentials.

name: Lucidity Demo
summary: A Nuxt consumer of Lucidity that proves headless reads: schemas, pages, and collections.
purpose: Reference frontend showing how a site consumes Lucidity’s query API for navigation and collections.
howItWorks:
The demo reads schema types from Lucidity, builds navigation from Pages, and loops included collections (for example posts on a Blog page) through the Lucidity query API.

It is a consumer, not the CMS authoring UI — that lives on the main Lucidity app.
architecture: Collection loops (e.g. posts) on composed pages
Reference integration for headless CMS consumption
features: List Lucidity schema types
Build nav from Pages
Render included collections such as blog posts
Demonstrate headless CMS consumption
Show how a Nuxt site pulls published Lucidity content
dataAuth: Uses Lucidity API keys/configuration to read published content. Does not replace CMS operator auth on the main Lucidity app.

name: Air Charter Broker CRM
summary: A Next.js + Supabase CRM for air-charter brokers: companies, contacts, and inquiries behind sign-in.
purpose: Give air-charter brokers a signed-in workspace to manage companies, contacts, and inbound inquiries with row-level security.
howItWorks:
A broker signs in and works with companies, contacts, and inquiries in a ShadCN-based UI.

Supabase RLS keeps each broker’s CRM rows scoped to authorised users so inquiry data is not globally public.
architecture: Row Level Security on CRM tables
features: Sign in to a broker workspace
Manage companies
Manage contacts
Track inquiries
Rely on RLS for data isolation
dataAuth: Supabase Auth identifies brokers. RLS policies restrict companies, contacts, and inquiries to authorised users. No public anonymous write access to CRM records.

name: TalkToMe
summary: AI meeting notes: record audio, transcribe with Whisper, summarise, file meetings in folders, and download an ICS event.
purpose: Turn spoken meetings into organised notes and calendar events for people who want capture → transcript → summary without a heavy enterprise suite.
howItWorks:
Record meeting audio in the app. Whisper produces a transcript, then an AI summary is generated.

Meetings are filed in folders for later retrieval. An ICS download creates a calendar event from the meeting.

Next.js powers the web app; Capacitor wraps an iOS build.
features: Record meeting audio
Transcribe with Whisper
Generate a meeting summary
File meetings in folders
Download an ICS calendar event
Use on web or iOS via Capacitor
dataAuth: Meeting audio, transcripts, summaries, and folder organisation are stored for the signed-in user. Calendar ICS is generated for download rather than forcing a cloud calendar credential into the docs.
integrations: OpenAI or summarisation provider as configured
deployment: Source on GitHub (jbiddulph/talktome). Next.js + Capacitor for web/iOS builds.
